analysis:
The PR adds a prompt-token cache. Rendered chat prompts are split at added-token boundaries, and per-piece token IDs are reused, keyed by SHA-256 over (scope, piece). Reuse is scoped by `promptCacheScope: cacheEnabled ? requestCacheScope : nil` (MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift patch near line 795). This mirrors the coordinator-authored prefix-KV cache scope from T-041, so a faster hit should not cross tenants. A nil scope takes the unchanged tokenizer path. The cache is also gated by the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch via `PromptTokenCachePolicy`.

Not verified: PromptTokenCache.swift (39b52ffc4553ca16:0) was supplied as metadata only, so I could not check scope derivation and hashing, memory bounds (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE_MB), eviction, concurrency, or the self-check and background-verify behavior. Cache-hit timing leaking prompt reuse within a single scope falls under the accepted SEC-035 same-account TTFT channel. In-memory cached prompt pieces are a new plaintext-derived (token ID) store in the provider process, within TB-003/T-014 exposure. This is not a new boundary, but its scope-partitioning and eviction need confirmation.

ChatTemplateLoopRewrites.swift: verbatim-matched, exactly-once string rewrites of the Gemma4 and GPT-OSS templates. They apply only on a unique match and only if the introduced variable names are absent, otherwise they are skipped. I traced all three rewrites against their comments and they look semantically equivalent. Correctness depends on the load-time and sampled self-checks, which I could not see. The rewrites are used only for the cache render. A template mismatch would affect prompt fidelity, not confidentiality.

LocalTokenizerLoader.swift: when the cache is enabled, the loader re-implements `AutoTokenizer.from(modelFolder:)` and constructs `PreTrainedTokenizer` directly. This may skip swift-transformers' class-specific tokenizer dispatch, which would change tokenization for some models. It is a correctness and consistency concern, not a demonstrated security regression, and it should be checked against the load-time self-check. The `effectiveContext` refactor is behavior-preserving.

PromptPreparationProbe.swift is a public benchmark seam only and exposes no new input path. The shown excerpt of the scheduler file (lines 1024-1514, event-stream forwarding) is unchanged by this PR.
